title: Uploading and Downloading Artifacts knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Uploading and Downloading Artifacts?
options: Upload and download actions move named files between workflow stages; paths and retention settings determine what evidence remains available.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Upload and download actions move named files between workflow stages; paths and retention settings determine what evidence remains available.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of uploading and downloading artifacts: Upload and download actions move named files between workflow stages; paths and retention settings determine what evidence remains available. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Uploading build outputs”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.
questions.explanation: Uploading build outputs: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to uploading and downloading artifacts?
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Upload and download actions move named files between workflow stages; paths and retention settings determine what evidence remains available. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
